html:
Ahilyabai Holkar ruled the Holkar state of Malwa in central India from 1767 to 1795. She is remembered as one of the best rulers of her century in India.

She was a village headman's daughter. Malhar Rao Holkar, a leading general of the Marathas, saw her as a child and married her to his son. Her husband was killed by a cannonball in 1754. Her father-in-law stopped her from burning herself on the pyre and trained her to run the state. He died in 1766 and her only son the year after, and she took the government herself.

She ruled from Maheshwar on the Narmada. Each day she sat in open court and heard anyone who came. She kept taxes light, did not seize the property of widows, and left command of the army to Tukoji Holkar, who was loyal to her for thirty years. Indore grew from a village into a rich town, and she settled weavers at Maheshwar whose saris are still made.

She spent her own fortune on temples, wells, river steps and rest houses for pilgrims all over India, far beyond her borders. In 1780 she rebuilt the Vishwanath temple at Varanasi, destroyed a century before.

A British officer who collected memories of her wrote that people of every class spoke of her as a saint.
sum: Ahilyabai Holkar ruled the Holkar state of Malwa in central India from 1767 to 1795. She is remembered as one of the best rulers of her century in India.
